comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 28, 2024, AMD had approximately 28,000 employees in its global workforce.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and AMD disclose their global workforce headcount as a primary human capital metric. Qualcomm reported approximately 49,000 employees across 37 countries, whereas AMD reported a smaller workforce of approximately 28,000 employees. Both companies describe their workforces as global but differ in geographic scale and total size.

sentences.text: At September 29, 2024, we had approximately 49,000 full-time, part-time and temporary workers, the overwhelming majority of which were full-time employees.
As of December 28, 2024, we had approximately 28,000 employees in our global workforce.

comparisons.peer_summary: In fiscal year 2024, the company's global voluntary attrition rate was approximately 2.9% (excluding VMware merger employees) and 6.2% (including them), both below the technology industry benchmark from AON's 2024 study.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Broadcom disclose their voluntary turnover/attrition rates for fiscal 2024. Qualcomm reported a voluntary turnover rate of approximately 5%. Broadcom reported global voluntary attrition rates of 2.9% (excluding VMware merger employees) and 6.2% (including them), noting both were below the technology industry benchmark. While both measure voluntary departure, Broadcom provides industry benchmark context and splits the metric by merger impact, whereas Qualcomm provides a single aggregate figure.

sentences.text: During fiscal 2024, our voluntary turnover rate was approximately 5%.

Our global voluntary attrition rates in fiscal year 2024 were approximately 2.9% (excluding employees who joined Broadcom as a result of the VMware Merger) and approximately 6.2% (including employees who joined Broadcom as a result of the VMware Merger), which are both below the technology industry benchmark (AON, 2024 Salary Increase and Turnover Study - Second Edition, September 2024).

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel faces significant competition for talent and limited hiring in 2024, with headcount actions expected to decrease the core workforce by approximately 15% by early 2025. Undesired turnover rates were 5.9% in 2024 and 5.6% in 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Intel disclose their voluntary (undesired) turnover rates for fiscal 2024. Qualcomm reported a voluntary turnover rate of approximately 5%. Intel reported an undesired turnover rate of 5.9%. Both metrics reflect similar levels of voluntary employee departure, though Intel's metric explicitly excludes retirees, divestitures, and job eliminations.

sentences.text: During fiscal 2024, our voluntary turnover rate was approximately 5%.

Our undesired turnover rate [footnote 1: Undesired turnover includes all regular Intel employees who voluntarily left Intel, but does not include Intel contract employees, interns, or employees who separated from Intel due to divestiture, retirement, voluntary separation packages, death, job elimination, or redeployment, or Mobileye and other non-integrated subsidiaries employees.] was 5.9% in 2024 and 5.6% in 2023.

comparisons.peer_summary: In fiscal year 2024, NVIDIA's overall turnover rate was 2.7%, reflecting the company's goal of being a place where employees build their careers over their lifetime.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and NVIDIA disclose their overall turnover rates for fiscal 2024. Qualcomm reported a voluntary turnover rate of approximately 5%, while NVIDIA reported a lower overall turnover rate of 2.7%. NVIDIA contextualizes its low rate by stating its goal is for employees to build careers over their lifetime and noting that employees 'tend to come and stay,' whereas Qualcomm does not provide this qualitative context for its 5% rate.
